title: Comparison of standard circular stapler anastomosis with or without circumferential suture enhancement in patients with robot-assisted Ivor-Lewis oesophagectomy due to malignant tumours of the oesophagus and oesophagogastric junction
summary: The STITCHES study is intended to investigate the benefit of additional suture reinforcement of the newly created connection between the esophagus and gastric tube during esophagectomy with a robotic assistance system in patients with malignant tumors of the esophagus and the transition to the stomach.

interventions.name: Standardised creation of the end-to-side oesophagogastrostomy with a circular stapler (double-row staple suture, size 25 to 29)
Standardised creation of the end-to-side oesophagogastrostomy with a circular stapler (double-row staple suture, size 25 to 29) and additional circular suture enhancement with absorbable sutures.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for robot-assisted esophageal resection with gastric pull-up and intrathoracic circular end-to-side anastomosis, esophageal carcinoma/cardiac carcinoma (AEG type 1 and 2), patient with or without prior neoadjuvant therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Person not capable of giving consent, pregnant/breastfeeding person, conversion during the surgery, malfunction of the stapler
